availability.p: The 1917 source is in the public domain in the United States. No new license is assigned to third-party digital source files by this conversion.

sourceDesc.p: Copy text: supplied ichneutae_ocr.txt, printed pp. 234–269. Structural comparison: supplied ichneutae_pearson_scaffold.xml. The opening two verses and opening note survive only in the scaffold; their printed page is inferred as 233. These are two transcriptions of the same edition, not independent textual witnesses. No page-image proofreading has been performed.

editorialDecl.p: Pearson’s fragment 314 is the main play. Pearson’s line numbers remain in n; corresp points to the supplied Hunt/Perseus reference. Short apparatus is separate from discursive commentary. OCR errors are corrected only where supported by the supplied material or unambiguous context. Unresolved readings use sic; OCR gaps differ from ancient losses. Brackets are retained as transcription signs and are not claimed to be a new diplomatic transcription. Dot runs give unspecified loss, not measured character counts. Missing numbered positions follow Pearson’s printed numbering and do not assert an exact papyrus extent.

Reference gap/aggregate pointers (especially Pearson 24–27, 379–386, and 395–430) identify a reference placeholder, not exact verse equivalence. Pearson 414 is a marginally attested reading and is not evidence that a continuous verse survives. Content and references to introductory pages outside the supplied OCR have not been reconstructed.
